topology_dependency: NONE in construction; premise law is topology-agnostic and may not name T1-T4 objects/scenarios.
positive_law: The whole image exists as one continuous interlaced fiber system made from long uninterrupted strands. People, environment and relationships emerge through changes in strand orientation, spacing, tension, crossing order and weave openness rather than through discrete marks, repeated modules, flat closed shapes or smooth modeled painting. Human specificity comes from stable body-scale weave rhythm and localized strand behavior. Present consequence/history appears as persistent pulled, shifted, rethreaded or tension-changed fiber relationships that remain part of the same continuous system.

axes.representation ontology: long continuous interlaced fibers/strands forming one connected representational fabric
axes.spatial/relational visual organization: over-under crossings, directional flow, tension and weave openness organize proximity/depth
axes.figure-ground/material-edge grammar: soft-to-firm fiber boundaries formed by strand convergence/divergence; no closed planar masses or discrete modules
axes.human identity/specificity mechanism: distinct body-scale strand cadence, crossing density, orientation and tension signature per person
axes.consequence/history representation: persistent rethreading, pull, slack/tension change or shifted crossing relation in the continuous fiber system
axes.tonal/texture/atmosphere construction: near-neutral tone from fiber density, overlap and shallow strand shadow rather than painterly deposits or smooth haze

anti_motif: Do not reduce the law to decorative textile texture laid over a conventional scene; fibers must be the actual representation substrate everywhere.
construction_exclusions: no topology-specific object, pose, architecture or scenario
